title: "![](/assets/node-icons/Pump.svg){height=20} Pump"
engine: julia
---

Pump water from a source node to a destination node.
The set flow rate will be pumped unless the intake storage is less than $10~m^3$,
in which case the flow rate will be linearly reduced to $0~m^3/s$.
The intake must be either a Basin or LevelBoundary.
When [PID controlled](/reference/node/pid-control.qmd), the pump must point away from the controlled basin in terms of links.

# Tables

## Static

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
include("../../../utils/gen_docs_table.jl")
const PUMP_RESTRICTIONS = Dict(:flow_rate => "non-negative")
table_from_schema(Ribasim.Schema.Pump.Static; restrictions = PUMP_RESTRICTIONS)
```

## Time

This table is the transient form of the `Pump` table.
With this all parameters can be updated over time. In between the given times the
values are block interpolated (forward fill), and outside the values are constant given by the
nearest time value.
Note that a `node_id` can be either in this table or in the static one, but not both.

```{julia}
# | code-fold: true
table_from_schema(Ribasim.Schema.Pump.Time; restrictions = PUMP_RESTRICTIONS)
```

# Equations

The behavior of a Pump is simple if these nodes are not PID controlled.
Their flow is given by a fixed flow rate $q$, multiplied by reduction factors:

$$
Q = \phi_\text{level} \, \mathrm{clamp}(\phi_\text{storage} Q_\text{set}, Q_{\min}, Q_{\max})
$$

- $Q$ is the actual Pump flow rate.
- $Q_\text{set}$ is the Pump's target `flow_rate`.
- $Q_{\min}$ and $Q_{\max}$ are the Pump `min_flow_rate` and `max_flow_rate`.
- $\phi_\text{storage}$ is the reduction factor that smoothly reduces flow when the upstream volume is below the equivalent of a water depth of $10 \;\text{cm}$ (change with solver setting `depth_threshold`).
- $\phi_\text{level}$ is the product of the reduction factors that smoothly reduce flow based on these criteria (change the $0.02 \;\text{m}$ with solver setting `level_difference_threshold`):
  - The upstream level is below `min_upstream_level` + $0.02 \;\text{m}$
  - The downstream level is above `max_downstream_level` - $0.02 \;\text{m}$

Since $\phi_\text{level}$ is applied after the clamp, `min_flow_rate` is not a strict minimum: the level criteria can still reduce the flow to zero.
